subject.title: sandbox: keep workspaceAccess none workspaces writable

question: Should `workspaceAccess: "none"` make the isolated sandbox `/workspace` writable by default while keeping the real agent workspace unmounted?
rationale: The source repro is clear, but the fix changes sandbox write semantics; a maintainer already rejected the strict tool-hiding workaround and routed the permanent contract decision back to this issue.

options.title: Approve isolated-writable none
options.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a coordinated mount, bridge, tool, docs, tests, and live-proof update.

options.title: Keep none read-only
options.body: Retain the current fail-closed behavior and update docs/support guidance so users choose `rw` or a future explicit writable mode for file-producing workflows.

options.title: Fold into bind-policy work
options.body: Resolve this together with https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59718 if maintainers want one broader least-privilege write model.

recommendation.title: Approve isolated-writable none
recommendation.body: Treat `none` as no real workspace access rather than no sandbox writes, and require a coordinated mount, bridge, tool, docs, tests, and live-proof update.

likelyOwner.reason: This person provided the latest maintainer direction on the adjacent PR and has recent merged history on the sandbox layout and mount boundary.
